hero.subtitle: When a loved one dies because of someone else's negligence on a Claremont road, the days that follow can feel impossible to navigate. LawProactive can connect your family with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death claims, at no cost to you.

about.title: Claremont Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Claremont saw 7 traffic deaths in the most recent reporting year, numbers that represent real families left to pick up the pieces. Corridors like Indian Hill Boulevard, Foothill Boulevard, Baseline Road, and the SR-210 stretch through town carry heavy weekday traffic, and Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. see the most reported collisions. When a crash on one of these roads takes a family member's life, California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim; if none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify. These cases run on a separate track from any criminal charges the responsible driver might face. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we simply listen to what happened, then connect grieving families in Claremont with an independent personal injury attorney who can explain your options and, if you choose, pursue a civil claim on a contingency basis.

items.title: Standing Rules Are Followed Carefully
items.desc: California limits who may file a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and moving to other dependents or heirs only if none exist. An independent attorney can confirm exactly where your family fits before any claim is filed.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Starts at Death
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity require much faster action. Reaching out early gives an attorney more time to gather crash records and witness accounts while they're still available.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Funeral Bill Can Be Recovered
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California can account for funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help lay out what your family's specific losses may include.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law prioritizes a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first. If none exist, other dependents or certain heirs may have standing instead. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and confirm who is eligible to bring the claim.

items.question: Does a criminal case against the driver affect our civil claim?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges the driver may face. Your family can pursue compensation through the civil courts regardless of the outcome of a criminal prosecution. An attorney can explain how the two processes may overlap or differ.

items.question: Our loved one died in a crash near the SR-210 and Indian Hill Boulevard area — does that change anything?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't change your legal rights, but the roadway involved can affect how evidence like traffic camera footage or CHP reports is gathered. If a government entity was involved, such as a road maintained by the city or state, the filing deadline may be much shorter than two years. An attorney can look into the specifics of where the crash happened and what deadlines apply.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and connecting with an independent attorney costs you nothing upfront. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your family recovers compensation.
